note: Source is the dictionary's own URL, CRAN package ltm (data(WIRS)); Rd_db('ltm')[['WIRS.Rd']] reproduces the card framing paragraph and all six item stems verbatim, numbered 'Item 1'..'Item 6', which are also the literal column headers of the ltm::WIRS data frame. Code derivation is POSITIONAL (data/ltm.R: names(x) <- paste('item_',1:ncol(x),sep='')), so the exemption was not claimed; instead the derivation was re-run. Every stored response equals the source cell at the same (row, column): per-respondent agreement is exactly 1.000 on all six diagonal cells (1005/1005 each) and at most 0.732 off-diagonal, and per-item means reproduce to 1e-10 (item_1 0.3731343284, item_2 0.5830845771, item_3 0.2825870647, item_4 0.2398009950, item_5 0.3572139303, item_6 0.1472636816). Step 3b PASSES: 6 items, resp {0,1}, and the WIRS consultation section has exactly 6 dichotomous items -- no other instrument is in this deposit. Deviations from literal transcription: none in wording; the Rd's indented 'Item N' headings were dropped as labels rather than shipped as part of item_text. option_text left blank on all rows (no published response labels or coding direction anywhere in the source; not invented). Single trivial section_id wirs_1, blank section_prompt; the card framing paragraph is whole-instrument and sits in instructions. Administered in English (UK survey), so no language/_translated columns. RIGHTS: the six question wordings are published in full in the GPL-2 ltm package's documentation and in Bartholomew et al.'s textbook; no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was located for the WIRS questions, and itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv has no row for WIRS or any workplace-relations instrument. No register row written (a round may not write ship rows).

note: English administration (US MTurk), so no language/_translated columns. Item text transcribed verbatim from the S1 Appendix Q28 matrix; the appendix's own statement numbers (1)/(2)/(3) tie directly to the source columns Q28_1/_2/_3, and data/witus_2022_narrator_perception.py renames those via an explicit dict to narrator_trustworthy/_comforting/_knowledgeable (no positional assignment). Trailing Qualtrics numbering ('(1)' etc.) stripped from item_text and option_text. option_text anchors 1=Not at all, 2=Only a little, 3=Moderately, 4=Very are printed as column headers with their codes in the same matrix. instructions holds Q28's own stem ('Please comment on the characteristics of the narrator'); the block-level framing Q20 ('The following questions are on the video that you watched.') was not recorded, as it frames a block containing other items not in this table. No named commercial instrument: these are the study's own three narrator-perception items, published in full in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE supplement -- no fee, no-redistribution or use-restriction clause from any rights holder is locatable, so nothing in the rights sections fires. Mapping verified cell-for-cell against the raw spreadsheet (route 9), all 12 item x resp cells exact.

note: mapping_basis=data_labels: the IRW item codes posaff1..posaff12 ARE the source .sav column names (data/wolf_2017_biodiversity_wellbeing.py melts [f'posaff{i}' for i in range(1,13)] with no rename), and each column carries its own SPSS variable label giving the adjective -- code-to-text is tied at the source, 12/12, no inference. Step 5b exemption is earned by the derivation pattern ('item IS the source column name'), not merely by mapping_basis. Value labels supplied the 1/5 anchors; '(1)'/'(5)' code echoes stripped, 2/3/4 left blank. instructions are canonical PANAS present-moment wording (level-3 source) because neither the .sav nor the PLOS article prints the administered instruction; item_text and option_text are entirely study_materials. Live responses are raw, not reverse-scored (paper: 'After reverse-scoring negative items...').
public_note: Despite the table name and dictionary description, these 12 items are a 12-adjective selection from the full PANAS and include six negative-affect adjectives (distressed, upset, guilty, scared, hostile, irritable) as well as six positive ones; the stored responses are raw, so the negative items must be reverse-scored before a positive-affect score is computed.
